bug_semantics: CWE-502 Java deserialization RCE in the deprecated fabric-sdk-java client. HFClient.deSerializeChannel(byte[]) / deSerializeChannel(File) wrap caller-supplied bytes in a raw ObjectInputStream and call readObject() with no ObjectInputFilter. Channel was made Serializable in the same change and implements a private readObject() that only defaultReadObject()s and rehydrates transients; that hook is not the entry point. An attacker who can feed crafted serialized bytes (compromised local channel file, SampleStore-style persistence, or any app that accepts Channel bytes) can instantiate gadget graphs during deserialization. Channel bytes are not sent by Fabric peers; this is a client-side sink. The GHSA snippet misplaces deSerializeChannel on Channel.java; the live method is on HFClient.java.
flaw_origin: First written in hyperledger/fabric-sdk-java commit 9282be96df6e5bd72d5aaca7b057b1693ae89af8 (FAB-6200 Java serialize channels, 2017-09-18) by rickr <cr22rc@gmail.com>. That non-merge Gerrit commit added Channel implements Serializable, Channel.readObject/serializeChannel, and HFClient.deSerializeChannel that does new ObjectInputStream(...).readObject() on the raw byte[]. Parent 24390b41241a5903378d6a1ffb6eb72db978f309 has none of those production APIs (Channel is a plain class). Later edits (FAB-6887 javadoc wrap, FAB-8074/FAB-8805) did not add a filter. No AI marker on the BIC commit object.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: GHSA-prf8-cf2x-rhx7 / CVE-2026-41586 describe unfiltered Java deserialization of Channel bytes in fabric-sdk-java. CVE.org remains PUBLISHED and NVD Analyzed, so this is not FALSE_POSITIVE. The live sink is HFClient.deSerializeChannel creating an unfiltered ObjectInputStream over caller bytes; Channel.readObject is the Serializable restoration hook added beside it. Attack path is client-side (local/serialized Channel bytes), matching the advisory. BIC search used git log -G/blame/-L on fabric-sdk-java (the GHSA's actual source), not an AI-marked commit hunt. 9282be96 is the smallest public commit that first wrote the deserialize API; the immediate parent tree lacks those lines. Later commits only rewrapped signatures or moved surrounding code; they did not introduce the mechanism and did not add ObjectInputFilter. AI judgment is BIC-only: 2017 human Gerrit author rickr, Signed-off-by self, no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot trailer. Closed NOT_AI with no fix SHA because the deprecated SDK was archived still vulnerable (unpatched object below); recommended closure is an ObjectInputFilter allowlist on that stream or migration to fabric-gateway.

potential_fix.approach: In HFClient.deSerializeChannel(byte[]), after constructing the ObjectInputStream and before readObject(), set an ObjectInputFilter allowlist such as org.hyperledger.fabric.sdk.*;java.util.*;java.lang.*;!* (as the GHSA sketches), or remove the Java-serialization persist/restore API and migrate callers to org.hyperledger.fabric:fabric-gateway.
potential_fix.rationale: The filter rejects non-allowlisted gadget classes before constructors and readObject hooks run, closing the CWE-502 RCE sink on this stream; dropping Java serialization removes the sink entirely.
